short: Gunboat diplomacy personified; he ran British foreign policy for three decades.
full:
Henry John Temple, Viscount Palmerston, was foreign secretary for most of the years between 1830 and 1851 before becoming prime minister in February 1855, aged seventy, brought in to salvage the Crimean War. He took the country to peace at Paris in 1856, fought the Second Opium War, and presided over the suppression of the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and the transfer of the East India Company's territories to the Crown.

His reputation rested on the aggressive assertion of British interests abroad. In the Don Pacifico affair of 1850 he blockaded Greece over one man's debts, and defended it with the claim that a British subject anywhere should be as safe as a Roman citizen once was. Returning to office in 1859, he kept Britain neutral in the American Civil War and blocked further parliamentary reform. He died in office in October 1865, the last prime minister to do so, and reform followed within two years.
